title: Curated match (series)
description: One row of data/curated/matches.jsonl: a best-of series, the middle level of the event -> match -> game grain (spec D1). A match exists because the series score is a source fact that counting games cannot recover — a forfeited or nullified series breaks that arithmetic — so the score lives here and never on a game. `sides` is always exactly two entries in the source's own column order: `sourceOrder` 1 is `MatchSchedule.Team1` and 2 is `Team2`. That is a position on the series row, **not** a game side: the recorded corpus has 52 game rows beside a series whose `Team1` is their `Team2`, so a match claims no blue/red side and only a game does. `isNullified` is always present; `forfeit` appears only when the source states one. The source's `Phase` and `Round` columns are null on every recorded match (measured, 65 of 65), so the round label is the source's `Tab`.

id.description: Opaque surrogate key derived from the source's MatchId (spec D3). The source id is carried in `source`.

overviewPage.description: The source page the match row came from.

bestOf.description: The series length the source declares (measured values: 1, 3 and 5). Absent when the source states none.

tab.description: The source's round label (ScoreboardGames-adjacent `Tab`): `Round 1`…`Round 5`, `Quarterfinals`, `Semifinals`, `Finals`, `Group A`, `Qualifiers`. Absent when the source has none.

patch.description: The patch the source states for the series, as text. Same numeric-truncation caveat as the game's `patch`.

forfeit.description: Present and true only when the source records `FF`. Measured absent on every recorded match, which is why no forfeit fixture exists yet.

isNullified.description: The source's IsNullified as stated: a nullified series is not the same as an unplayed one.

sourceOrder.description: The source's column: 1 for `MatchSchedule.Team1`, 2 for `Team2`. A position on the series row, not a game side — never read it as blue/red.

seriesScore.description: The series score for this side as the source states it. Absent when the source has no score.

winnerTeamId.description: Absent only when the source states no winner.

matchId.description: MatchSchedule.MatchId. Like GameId it embeds its page (`2023 Season World Championship/Play-In_Round 1_4`), and it is the same string a game row carries, so a game and its series can be re-joined by hand.
